children: Oil futures rise sharply as the U.S. launches new strikes against Iranian targets and President Trump warns "they will be hit at a much harder and higher level" if Iran retaliates against the latest "justified attack." WTI settles up 5.2% at $90.22 a barrel, its highest close since July 23. "While the escalated conflict in the Middle East continues to slow Strait of Hormuz traffic, along with the continued global tightness in diesel fuel, the near-term path of least resistance for oil prices still looks higher," Dennis Kissler of BOK Financial says in a note. Brent rises 4.6% to $94.65 a barrel. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
